タコライス.summary: A local dish born in Okinawa: rice topped with taco fillings such as spiced ground meat, cheese, lettuce and tomato, with salsa. It is said to have been created at a restaurant in Kin, home to a US military base, to give American soldiers a cheap, filling meal. Rice and taco fillings go together surprisingly well. It is now so familiar it is served in Okinawan school lunches. Many shops across the prefecture serve it.

shops.name: King Tacos Kin Honten
shops.query: キングタコス 金武本店
shops.comment: Carries on from the shop where taco rice was born; generous portions.

shops.name: Taco Rice Cafe Kijimunaa Sakurazaka
shops.query: タコライスcafe きじむなぁ 国際通り桜坂店
shops.comment: Known for its omelet-topped Omu-Taco.

ポークたまごおにぎり.summary: An Okinawan favorite: grilled pork luncheon meat and an omelette sandwiched in rice and wrapped in nori. It is a staple breakfast and light meal in Okinawa. The salty pork and gentle omelette go well with rice. Versions with extras such as miso, fried shrimp or bitter melon tempura are also popular. Specialty shops near Naha's Makishi Public Market draw lines. You can also easily buy them at convenience stores. They are perfect for breakfast on a trip.

shops.name: Pork Tamago Onigiri Honten Makishi
shops.query: ポークたまごおにぎり本店 牧志
shops.comment: A specialist that opens early; expect a line.

shops.name: Potama Naha Airport
shops.query: ポーたま 那覇空港
shops.comment: In the domestic arrivals lobby.

沖縄タコス.summary: Tacos that spread in Okinawa under the influence of US base culture. Crisp fried tortillas are filled with spiced ground meat, cheese, lettuce and tomato, and topped with salsa. Based on American tacos, they have long been a familiar dish in Okinawa. The crunchy shells, juicy filling and spicy sauce are a fun combination. Try them at shops in Koza (Okinawa City), Kin and elsewhere. They make a great casual meal.

shops.name: Charlie's Tacos Honten
shops.query: チャーリー多幸寿 本店 沖縄市
shops.comment: A taco shop born under postwar US rule.

shops.name: King Tacos Kin Honten
shops.query: キングタコス 金武本店 タコス
shops.comment: Its tacos are popular too; a landmark of this base town.

ゴーヤーチャンプルー.summary: The classic Okinawan home dish: bitter melon stir-fried with island tofu, pork or luncheon meat and egg. Champuru means mixed together in the Okinawan language. The slight bitterness of goya, firm island tofu and gentle egg are addictive together. Goya is loved as a nutritious vegetable for getting through hot summers. It is a standard menu item at Okinawan diners and izakaya. It goes well with both rice and awamori.

shops.name: Yunangi
shops.query: ゆうなんぎい 那覇
shops.comment: A long-established Okinawan home-cooking restaurant.

shops.name: Hanagasa Shokudo
shops.query: 花笠食堂 那覇
shops.comment: An old-style diner with many set meals.

ラフテー.summary: A traditional Okinawan dish of skin-on pork belly slowly simmered with awamori, brown sugar and soy sauce. It is simmered until tender enough to cut with chopsticks, with a melting texture and a rich sweet-savory flavor. It is said to have been eaten as court cuisine in the days of the Ryukyu Kingdom. Awamori softens the meat and removes any odor. Try it at restaurants and izakaya in Okinawa. It is sometimes served on Okinawa soba and goes perfectly with awamori.

shops.name: Yunangi
shops.query: ゆうなんぎい 那覇 ラフテー
shops.comment: Famous for its melt-in-the-mouth rafute.

shops.name: Urizun
shops.query: うりずん 栄町 那覇
shops.comment: Founded in the Showa era; aged awamori and Ryukyu cuisine.

沖縄そば.summary: Okinawa's signature noodle dish. Though called soba, it uses no buckwheat; the thick noodles are made from wheat flour. The broth, made from pork bones and bonito flakes, is light yet rich, topped with pork belly, kamaboko and green onion. The Okinawan way is to change the flavor with pickled ginger or koregusu, chili peppers steeped in awamori. There are countless Okinawa soba shops across the prefecture. Enjoy the differences in noodles and broth from shop to shop.

shops.name: Kishimoto Shokudo Honten
shops.query: きしもと食堂 本店 本部
shops.comment: Founded in the Meiji era; hand-made noodles using wood ash.

shops.name: Kishimoto Shokudo Yaedake
shops.query: きしもと食堂 八重岳店
shops.comment: A short drive from the main shop.

ソーキそば.summary: Okinawa soba topped with soki, pork spare ribs simmered sweet and savory. There are nankotsu soki, simmered until even the cartilage is edible, and hon soki, with the bone in. The meltingly tender meat and rich sweet-savory flavor go well with the light broth. Filling and satisfying, it is one of the most popular kinds of Okinawa soba. Many Okinawa soba shops serve it. Adding koregusu chili is also recommended.

shops.name: Gabusoka Shokudo Honten
shops.query: 我部祖河食堂 本店 名護
shops.comment: The originator of soki soba.

shops.name: Gabusoka Shokudo Shuri
shops.query: 我部祖河食堂 首里店
shops.comment: A branch in Naha.

海ぶどう.summary: A seaweed from Okinawan waters, named sea grapes because its tiny beads are clustered like bunches of grapes. It is also called green caviar. In the mouth, the beads pop, with a faint ocean aroma and saltiness. The standard way is to eat it with ponzu or vinegar dressing, and some shops serve sea grape rice bowls. Keeping it in the fridge makes the beads shrivel, so store it at room temperature. Try it at izakaya and restaurants in Okinawa.

shops.name: Ganso Umibudo
shops.query: 元祖 海ぶどう 恩納村
shops.comment: The shop that created the umibudo rice bowl.

shops.name: Onna no Eki Nakayukui Market
shops.query: おんなの駅 なかゆくい市場
shops.comment: Onna's farmers' market; sells umibudo too.

ジーマーミ豆腐.summary: A traditional Okinawan dish of jimami, peanut, milk mixed with sweet potato starch and kneaded until set. Despite the name tofu, it contains no soybeans. It features a chewy bounce, a smooth texture and the rich, sweet flavor of peanuts. The standard way is to eat it with a slightly sweet soy-based sauce. It is said to have been made as court cuisine in the Ryukyu Kingdom. It is served at restaurants and sold at souvenir shops in Okinawa. Its chewy texture is addictive.

shops.name: Yunangi
shops.query: ゆうなんぎい 那覇 ジーマーミ豆腐
shops.comment: Has the full range of local dishes.

shops.name: Urizun
shops.query: うりずん 栄町 ジーマーミ豆腐
shops.comment: A long-established Ryukyu-cuisine izakaya.

ミミガーさしみ.summary: Mimiga means pig's ear in the Okinawan language. Mimiga sashimi is boiled pig's ear cut into thin strips and dressed with vinegared miso, peanut sauce or ponzu. Enjoy the crunchy cartilage and jiggly skin. It represents Okinawa's pork culture, where people are said to eat every part of the pig except its squeal. Low in fat and refreshing, it is perfect with awamori or beer. It is a standard dish at Okinawan izakaya.

shops.name: Yunangi
shops.query: ゆうなんぎい 那覇 ミミガー
shops.comment: A long-established Okinawan home-cooking restaurant.

shops.name: Urizun
shops.query: うりずん 栄町 ミミガー
shops.comment: A good match for awamori.

足ティビチ.summary: In Okinawan, pig's feet are called tibichi. Ashi tibichi is pig's feet simmered for a long time with bonito dashi, awamori and soy sauce. It features meltingly soft skin and a jiggly gelatinous texture. It is often served as a soup simmered with daikon and kelp, or as an oden ingredient. Full of collagen, it is loved by locals. Try it at Okinawan diners and oden restaurants.

shops.name: Hanagasa Shokudo
shops.query: 花笠食堂 てびち
shops.comment: A diner that began as a tebichi specialist.

shops.name: Machigwa no Shokudo Dotonbori
shops.query: 道頓堀 牧志公設市場 てびち
shops.comment: A diner on the second floor of the public market.

豆腐よう.summary: A traditional Okinawan delicacy: island tofu dried, then soaked in a marinade of red yeast rice and awamori and aged for a long time. It features a vivid red color and a smooth, rich, cheese-like texture. It is said to have been made as court cuisine in the Ryukyu Kingdom, based on a dish from China. The standard way is to scrape off a little at a time with a toothpick and enjoy it with awamori. It is sold at souvenir shops in Okinawa. Even a small amount is intensely flavorful.

shops.name: Benihama Tofuyo
shops.query: 紅濱 唐芙蓉 豆腐よう
shops.comment: Tofuyo fermented with red koji.

shops.name: Ryu no Kura
shops.query: 龍の蔵 豆腐よう 県庁前
shops.comment: A tofuyo specialist that ages it in a limestone cave.

サーターアンダーギー.summary: Okinawa's signature fried sweet. In Okinawan, sata means sugar and andagi means deep-fried. A dough of flour, sugar and eggs is rolled into balls and fried, crisp outside and moist inside. When fried, the surface cracks open like a blooming flower, so it is considered lucky and made for celebrations too. There are also brown sugar and purple sweet potato flavors. They are sold all over Okinawa. They are especially good warm, fresh from the fryer.

shops.name: Ayumi Sata Andagi
shops.query: 歩 サーターアンダギー 牧志
shops.comment: A specialist inside the public market.

shops.name: Sata Andagi no Mise Amuro
shops.query: さーたーあんだーぎーの店 安室 首里
shops.comment: A Shuri specialist; brown-sugar and purple-yam flavors too.

ちんすこう.summary: Okinawa's signature traditional sweet: a baked cookie of flour, sugar and lard. It features a light, crumbly texture and a simple, gentle sweetness. It is said to have been made as a court sweet in the Ryukyu Kingdom. Today there are many flavors, such as salt, brown sugar, purple sweet potato, pineapple and chocolate. Many are individually wrapped and easy to share, making them a classic Okinawan souvenir. They are widely sold at souvenir shops.

shops.name: Honke Arakaki Kashiten
shops.query: 本家 新垣菓子店 ちんすこう
shops.comment: From a family of Ryukyu royal cooks; order ahead.

shops.name: Arakaki Chinsuko Honpo Makishi
shops.query: 新垣ちんすこう本舗 国際通り牧志店
shops.comment: Available on Kokusai-dori.

紅いもタルト.summary: One of Okinawa's best-known souvenir sweets, made with beni imo, the local purple sweet potato. Vivid purple sweet potato paste is piped into boat-shaped tart shells and baked. Enjoy the natural, gentle sweetness of the potato with the crisp tart. It is said to have been created by a confectioner in Yomitan to promote the village. Its colorful look and Okinawan feel add to its popularity. It is sold at Naha Airport and souvenir shops across the prefecture.

shops.name: Okashi Goten Yomitan Honten
shops.query: 御菓子御殿 読谷本店
shops.comment: The originator of the purple-yam tart.

shops.name: Okashi Goten Kokusai-dori Matsuo
shops.query: 御菓子御殿 国際通り松尾店
shops.comment: Available in Naha.

沖縄ぜんざい.summary: In Okinawa, zenzai is not warm red bean soup but cold shaved ice. Kintoki beans simmered sweet with brown sugar go into a bowl, topped with plenty of fluffy shaved ice. Enjoy the rich sweetness of brown sugar, the soft beans and the cool ice together. Many shops add shiratama rice dumplings. In hot Okinawa, it is a familiar snack eaten all year. Try it at diners and zenzai specialty shops. It is perfect for a break on a hot day.

shops.name: Fujiya Tomari Honten
shops.query: 富士家 泊本店 ぜんざい
shops.comment: The go-to Okinawan zenzai shop.

shops.name: Sennichi
shops.query: 千日 那覇 ぜんざい
shops.comment: Opened shortly after the war.
